1. Core Clinical Tension: A 30-year-old HIV-positive woman with variable antiretroviral adherence presents with new ulcerative lesions across the upper and lower extremities despite an undetectable HIV viral load. The tension lies in determining whether the lesions represent an opportunistic cutaneous infection failing immunologic control versus a refractory, relapsing parasitic ulceration exacerbated by prior interrupted courses of therapy.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Day 1 clinical triage ends after documentation of the new limb ulcers and baseline lab assessment confirming an undetectable HIV status, immediately prior to dermal biopsy and parasite isolation.
3. Differential Distinctions: A simple opportunistic infection due to viremic HIV failure is ruled out by virologic suppression. Secondary bacterial pyoderma is differentiated by Giemsa-stained scrapings and tissue biopsy yielding parasite isolation BG03.
case_prompt:
A 30-year-old female patient diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in 2010 presented for clinical evaluation due to new cutaneous ulcerations. She had a history of intermittent antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, and efavirenz) that had been discontinued several times. 

One year prior to presentation, she developed a solitary ulcerated lesion on her lower extremity for which she received systemic antimicrobial therapy for 20 days before stopping treatment prematurely. In late 2021, she returned with new ulcerative skin lesions involving the left lower limb and the right upper limb. Routine laboratory assessment confirmed an undetectable HIV status.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Opportunistic Cutaneous Infection Secondary to Uncontrolled HIV Viremia
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the patient's established HIV history and frequent interruptions of antiretroviral therapy. Ruled out by laboratory confirmation of viral suppression at re-presentation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In late 2021, she returned to hospital service with HIV-undetectable status, but new lesions on the left lower limb and right upper limb.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Incompletely Treated Initial Ulceration / Treatment Failure
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the patient's history of premature discontinuation of systemic therapy, leading to recurrent disease rather than new unrelated bacterial dermatitis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: She was treated daily with a dose of meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime ) at 20 mg/Sb+5/kg administered intravenously for 20 days but discontinued the treatment soon after.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic pivot was achieved by performing a skin biopsy for parasite isolation, yielding clinical isolate BG03 and confirming the parasitic etiology responsible for the recurrent cutaneous disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: At that time, a biopsy sample was collected for parasite isolation, resulting in the obtaining of the clinical isolate denominated as BG03.

editor_comments: Case accurately abstracts tegumentary presentation of L. infantum in an HIV patient without pre-revealing parasitic isolation or species identification.
